Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

Hospital Course:
The patient, a 69-year-old male with a known duodenal diverticulum and remote history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery, was admitted to the hospital with bilateral upper quadrant abdominal pain for several weeks, nausea, abdominal distension, and food intolerance. A CT scan revealed a distended gastric remnant and a possible bowel obstruction.

The patient was taken to the operating room for an exploratory laparotomy where a 4.5 cm enterolith was found and removed from the distal jejunum. A cholecystectomy was also performed during which gallstones were discovered. The patient had an uneventful recovery and was discharged on postoperative day 8.

Follow-up:
At the patient's postoperative visit, two weeks after surgery, he was reported to be in good health. Unfortunately, the patient was lost to follow-up after one month.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Summary:
This 69-year-old male presented with bilateral upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, abdominal distension, and food intolerance. He was found to have a distended gastric remnant and a bowel obstruction caused by a 4.5 cm enterolith containing bile salts. Treatment included an exploratory laparotomy and enterolith removal, as well as a cholecystectomy. The patient had an uneventful recovery and was discharged on postoperative day 8. It is unfortunate that the patient was lost to follow-up after one month.

text:
# Principal diagnosis: **K56.4 Other impaction of intestine (enterolith)**

**Why this code**
- The condition that prompted admission and surgery was small bowel obstruction in the distal jejunum. It was caused by a 4.5 cm enterolith, which was removed at laparotomy.
- In ICD-10-AM, obstruction from an enterolith is indexed to **K56.4**.
- **K56.3 (gallstone ileus) is not appropriate.** The obstruction was caused by a true enterolith containing bile salts. These typically form from stasis, here likely from the duodenal diverticulum and altered post-bypass anatomy. Gallstone ileus requires a gallstone passing through a biliary-enteric fistula, and none was documented.

**Likely additional diagnoses**
- **K80.20** Calculus of gallbladder without cholecystitis, without obstruction. This supports the cholecystectomy.
- **K57.10** Diverticular disease of small intestine (duodenal diverticulum) without perforation or abscess, without bleeding.
- **Z98.0** Intestinal bypass and anastomosis status (previous Roux-en-Y gastric bypass).

**Likely procedures**
- Laparotomy with removal of the enterolith from the jejunum (enterotomy).
- Cholecystectomy.

The procedures would be coded with ACHI codes according to the operative approach. Please confirm all codes against the ICD-10-AM/ACHI edition in use and any local coding standards.
